context: OpenCode only discovers agents, commands and skills from standard locations (.opencode/agent|command|skill for a project, ~/.config/opencode/... for global). SYSTEM-ENGINEERING defines the contracts in AGENTS/*/agent.json, COMMANDS/commands.json and SKILLS/. Restriction: no dependence on OpenCode reading arbitrary folders, and every agent must come from a contract. ADR-0015 adopted an adapter-only bridge.
problem: How are OpenCode assets produced from the contracts so they live in discoverable locations, stay versioned, and never drift from the source of truth?

pros: Generated assets are committed and reviewable

cons: Agents not guaranteed to match contracts

decision: Implement a generation pipeline owned by `se adapter opencode`. Every OpenCode agent (.opencode/agent/<role>.md) is generated from AGENTS/*/agent.json; every command (.opencode/command/<cmd>.md) from COMMANDS/commands.json (body wraps se.py); every skill from SKILLS/. Generated assets are committed. opencode.json and AGENTS.md are generated from contracts, policies and docs. `se validate` recomputes a hash of each contract against its generated asset and reports drift.
reason: It guarantees every agent comes from a contract (restriction 5), uses only standard OpenCode discovery locations (restriction 4), keeps one source of truth, and makes drift detectable in CI.
consequences: SCRIPTS/se_core gains an adapter module. TESTS must cover round-trip (contract -> generated -> schema valid). Contract changes require regeneration; drift is a validation failure.
